title: Mutual authentication deprecated — consider ztunnel encryption

detection.reason: Cilium network policies (CiliumNetworkPolicy / CiliumClusterwideNetworkPolicy) are not collected — run the command to list the affected policies

quote: gs_mutual_authentication support is now deprecated and will be removed in a future version.
remediation: Policies the command lists use `authentication.mode: required`; plan the move to ztunnel-based encryption.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ciliumnetworkpolicies.cilium.io,ciliumclusterwidenetworkpolicies.cilium.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | . as $p | [(.spec // empty), (.specs[]?)] | map(((.ingress // []) + (.egress // []) + (.ingressDeny // []) + (.egressDeny // []))[]) | select(any(.[]; .authentication.mode? == "required")) | $p | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row relies on mutual authentication

title: Envoy Go Extensions (proxylib) and Kafka-aware policies removed

detection.reason: Cilium network policies (CiliumNetworkPolicy / CiliumClusterwideNetworkPolicy) are not collected — run the command to list the affected policies

quote: Envoy Go Extensions (proxylib) was removed after deprecation in Cilium 1.18.
remediation: Remove the `rules` section (with `kafka`, `l7` or `l7proto`) from every policy the command lists BEFORE upgrading; Kafka-aware and other proxylib L7 policies are not enforced by 1.20.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ciliumnetworkpolicies.cilium.io,ciliumclusterwidenetworkpolicies.cilium.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | . as $p | [(.spec // empty), (.specs[]?)] | map(((.ingress // []) + (.egress // []) + (.ingressDeny // []) + (.egressDeny // []))[]) | select(any(.[]; (.toPorts // []) | any(.rules != null and (.rules | has("kafka") or has("l7") or has("l7proto"))))) | $p | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row must lose its proxylib rules
coversNotes: Changes to Features / Removed Options: Support for Envoy Go Extensions (proxylib)

title: `CiliumNodeConfig` v2alpha1 removed — use `cilium.io/v2`

detection.reason: CiliumNodeConfig is not collected

quote: If you are still using the `v2alpha1` API version of `CiliumNodeConfig`, update existing manifests or tooling that references `cilium.io/v2alpha1` to use `cilium.io/v2` instead.
remediation: Rewrite every CiliumNodeConfig manifest (Git, GitOps, scripts) to `apiVersion: cilium.io/v2` before upgrading; the command lists objects last written as v2alpha1. Applying a v2alpha1 manifest fails on 1.20.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ciliumnodeconfigs.cilium.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(any(.metadata.managedFields[]?; .apiVersion == "cilium.io/v2alpha1")) | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row was last written with cilium.io/v2alpha1
coversNotes: Changes to Features / Removed Options: The `v2alpha1` API version of `CiliumNodeConfig`

title: CNI spec version `1.0.0` by default — update custom CNI configs

detection.reason: the option's VALUE is not collected (cilium-config ships key names only); the chart writes custom-cni-conf: "false" on every install

quote: Cilium updated to use CNI standard `v1.0.0` by default.
remediation: Affected only if the command prints `custom-cni-conf=true` (you maintain the CNI configuration yourself): set its `cniVersion` to `1.0.0` before upgrading. `false` (the chart default) needs nothing. `cni-chaining-mode=aws-cni` (chained to the AWS VPC CNI) is not affected either: Cilium builds its file from the VPC CNI's own `10-aws.conflist` and keeps that file's `cniVersion`.
verifyCommand: kubectl get configmap -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name == "cilium-config") | .data | to_entries[] | select(.key | test("^(custom-cni-conf|cni-chaining-mode)$")) | "\(.key)=\(.value)"'  # custom-cni-conf=true means you maintain the CNI config; cni-chaining-mode=aws-cni keeps the VPC CNI's cniVersion

title: Gateway API v1.6.1+ required — install Experimental TLSRoute or existing TLSRoutes disappear

detection.reason: checked the Gateway API CRDs' bundle-version annotation — a bundle below v1.6.1 must be upgraded first; a required CRD that is not installed at all is caught by rtz-cilium-1.20-gateway-api-v1-crds-required's command

quote: Cilium's Gateway API support now requires Gateway API v1.6.1 at a minimum to work correctly.
remediation: Upgrade the Gateway API CRDs named to v1.6.1 BEFORE Cilium 1.20. If you use TLSRoute, back the objects up and install the EXPERIMENTAL TLSRoute CRD from v1.6.1 (it still serves v1alpha2) — the Standard one makes existing TLSRoute objects unreadable from etcd, i.e. they vanish.
verifyCommand: kubectl get crd -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.group == "gateway.networking.k8s.io") | "\(.metadata.name) bundle=\(.metadata.annotations["gateway.networking.k8s.io/bundle-version"] // "?") channel=\(.metadata.annotations["gateway.networking.k8s.io/channel"] // "?") served=\([.spec.versions[] | select(.served) | .name] | join(","))"'  # bundles below v1.6.1 must be upgraded; TLSRoute must be the experimental channel

gate.reason: only clusters with Cilium's Gateway API support enabled are affected

title: Gateway API: GRPCRoute, TLSRoute, ReferenceGrant and BackendTLSPolicy CRDs must serve `v1`

detection.reason: reads the installed Gateway API CRDs' served versions; a CRD that is not installed at all is not judged — the command prints it as MISSING

quote: Cilium's Gateway API support now requires Gateway API v1.6.1 at a minimum to work correctly.
remediation: Cilium 1.20's operator requires GatewayClass, Gateway, HTTPRoute, GRPCRoute, TLSRoute, ReferenceGrant and BackendTLSPolicy, all served at `v1`; the CRDs named do not serve it, and any the command prints as MISSING must be installed too. Install the Gateway API v1.6.1 CRDs (TLSRoute from the EXPERIMENTAL channel if you have TLSRoute objects — see rtz-cilium-1.20-gateway-api-1-6-1-required) before upgrading Cilium.
verifyCommand: kubectl get crd -o json | jq -r '(.items | map({key: .metadata.name, value: ([.spec.versions[] | select(.served) | .name] | join(","))}) | from_entries) as $c | ["gatewayclasses","gateways","httproutes","grpcroutes","tlsroutes","referencegrants","backendtlspolicies"][] | (. + ".gateway.networking.k8s.io") as $n | "\($n) \($c[$n] // "MISSING")"'  # every row must list v1; MISSING or no v1 disables the Cilium Gateway API support

gate.reason: only clusters with Cilium's Gateway API support enabled are affected

title: `cec.cilium.io/*` Gateway infrastructure annotations no longer reach CiliumEnvoyConfig (from 1.20.3)

detection.reason: Gateway infrastructure metadata is not collected

quote: Annotations in the `cec.cilium.io/*` namespace supplied through Gateway or GAMMA infrastructure metadata are no longer propagated to internally generated `CiliumEnvoyConfig` resources.
remediation: If a Gateway's `spec.infrastructure.annotations` sets `cec.cilium.io/*` keys to change proxy or policy behaviour, that stops working; configure the behaviour on the CiliumEnvoyConfig or the Gateway API resources directly.

title: Policies with neither `spec` nor `specs` are rejected at admission

detection.reason: Cilium network policies (CiliumNetworkPolicy / CiliumClusterwideNetworkPolicy) are not collected — run the command to list the affected policies

quote: CiliumNetworkPolicy and CiliumClusterwideNetworkPolicy resources that specify neither `spec` nor `specs` are now rejected at admission time by the Kubernetes API server via a CEL validation rule.
remediation: Existing empty policies stay, but re-applying them (GitOps sync) fails. Delete or fill each policy the command lists.

title: Cluster Mesh MCS-API: self-managed ServiceExport / ServiceImport CRDs must serve `v1beta1`

detection.reason: the option's VALUE is not collected (cilium-config ships key names only); the chart writes clustermesh-enable-mcs-api and clustermesh-mcs-api-install-crds on every install

quote: Cilium MCS-API implementation now uses the `v1beta1` version of the MCS-API CRDs.
remediation: Affected only if the command prints `clustermesh-enable-mcs-api=true` with `clustermesh-mcs-api-install-crds=false` (you install the MCS-API CRDs yourself): the 1.20 operator then requires ServiceExport and ServiceImport served at `v1beta1` and reports "Required MCS-API resources are not found" otherwise, so MCS-API support does not start. Install the mcs-api CRDs that serve `v1beta1` before upgrading. With `install-crds=true` (the chart default) the operator updates the CRDs itself and the upgrade is transparent, as upstream says.
verifyCommand: kubectl get configmap -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name == "cilium-config") | .data | to_entries[] | select(.key | test("^(clustermesh-enable-mcs-api|clustermesh-mcs-api-install-crds)$")) | "\(.key)=\(.value)"'  # enable=true with install-crds=false is affected

title: Auto-generated Cluster Mesh certificates now valid one year — renewed only on chart re-render

detection.reason: certificate lifetimes of chart-generated Secrets are not collected

quote: Make sure to upgrade Cilium at least once per year to prevent the certificates from expiring
remediation: With the default `helm` generation method, Cluster Mesh certificates generated by 1.20 expire after a year unless the chart is re-rendered. Upgrade at least yearly, switch to `cronJob` / `certmanager`, or set `clustermesh.apiserver.tls.auto.certValidityDuration`.
verifyCommand: kubectl get secret -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("^clustermesh-apiserver-(server|admin|remote|client)-cert$")) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name)"'  # then: kubectl get secret NAME -n NS -o jsonpath='{.data.tls\.crt}' | base64 -d | openssl x509 -noout -enddate

title: certgen now fails when the CA expires before the leaf certificates

detection.reason: CA expiry is inside a Secret's data

quote: now defaults to enforcing that the CA chain remains valid for the entire duration of the leaf certificates to be generated, and fails with a hard error if that is not the case.
remediation: In `cronJob` mode, check the `cilium-ca` expiry: if it ends before a newly generated leaf would, regenerate the CA first or the certgen Job fails and certificates stop rotating. `certgen.enforceCAValidityThroughoutLeavesDuration=false` disables the check.
verifyCommand: kubectl get secret -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name == "cilium-ca") | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name)"'  # then: kubectl get secret cilium-ca -n NS -o jsonpath='{.data.ca\.crt}' | base64 -d | openssl x509 -noout -enddate

title: KPR without socket LB: NodePort traffic is load-balanced at the client — NetworkPolicy must allow the backends

detection.reason: the option's VALUE is not collected (cilium-config ships key names only)

quote: The client pod's NetworkPolicy consequently needs to allow egress traffic towards the service's backends, and the backends' NetworkPolicy needs to allow ingress traffic by the client pod.
remediation: If cilium-config has `kube-proxy-replacement: "true"` with `bpf-lb-sock: "false"` or `bpf-lb-sock-hostns-only: "true"`, in-cluster calls to NodePort Services are now translated at the client: allow client egress to the backend Pods and backend ingress from the clients before upgrading, or those calls are dropped.
verifyCommand: kubectl get configmap -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name == "cilium-config") | .data | to_entries[] | select(.key | test("^(kube-proxy-replacement|bpf-lb-sock|bpf-lb-sock-hostns-only)$")) | "\(.key)=\(.value)"'  # KPR true with socket LB off or host-namespace-only is affected
